name: Caleb Mercer, Step-Down: DKA after stopping basal insulin during a viral illness (in class)

caseMeta.title: In-class DKA: sick-day basal insulin omission during a viral illness, moderate-to-severe DKA in a young adult with type 1 diabetes (36 hours, checkpoints every 4 hours)
learningObjectives: Recognize DKA triggered by stopping basal insulin during an illness ("no food, no insulin"), and confirm the diagnosis and severity with glucose, beta-hydroxybutyrate, pH, bicarbonate and the anion gap.

Manage an adult DKA protocol (2024 consensus) safely: isotonic fluids, fixed-rate insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h, a separate dextrose line when glucose is under 250, peripheral potassium limits (riders, 10 mEq/h, 20 mEq/L), holding insulin for K under 3.5, magnesium, and the resolution criteria.
Check every handoff, line, site and order against the newest results and the protocol: potassium limits, the dextrose line, IV sites and the transition rules.

Carry out the transition with basal insulin at least 2 hours before stopping the drip, discontinue droplet precautions when the viral panel is negative, and teach sick-day rules with teach-back and complete discharge supplies.

problems.name: Moderate-to-severe diabetic ketoacidosis
problems.details: pH 7.18, bicarbonate 8, anion gap 28, beta-hydroxybutyrate 6.4, glucose 538 (0145). Fixed-rate insulin 7.6 units/h from 0305 (no bolus); 0.9% saline (no potassium in the bags); potassium by peripheral riders.

problems.name: Type 1 diabetes since 2014 on injections; stopped basal insulin while ill (no written sick-day plan)
problems.details: Glargine 24 units at 2100 (last Fri 2100), lispro 1 unit/10 g + 1 unit/50 above 150. HbA1c 8.1% (10/2026).

problems.name: Hypokalemia on treatment (K 3.2 at 1400) and hypomagnesemia (Mg 1.6)

orders.name: Droplet precautions (influenza-like illness; respiratory viral panel pending)
orders.instructions: Surgical mask on the patient outside the room and for transport. Staff wear a surgical mask within 6 feet; hand hygiene; door sign. RN may discontinue per the respiratory isolation protocol when the respiratory viral panel is negative for influenza A/B, SARS-CoV-2 and RSV and the patient is afebrile.
orders.rationale: Fever, cough, sore throat and body aches for 5 days; respiratory viral panel sent 0150.

orders.name: NPO except ice chips and sips of water
orders.instructions: Vomiting. Advance when nausea settles.

orders.name: ED labs: venous blood gas, BMP, magnesium, phosphorus, beta-hydroxybutyrate, CBC with differential, lactate, lipase, hepatic panel, serum osmolality, HbA1c, urinalysis; POC glucose; respiratory viral panel PCR (influenza A/B, SARS-CoV-2, RSV)

orders.instructions: Give 4 mg IV Once.
orders.rationale: Vomiting since Sunday.

orders.name: sodium chloride 0.9% bolus (ED)
orders.instructions: Give 1,000 mL over 1 hour IV Once.
orders.rationale: DKA with volume loss: 1,000 mL / 76.0 kg = 13.2 mL/kg in the first hour.

orders.name: acetaminophen (OFIRMEV) injection 1,000 mg in 100 mL (ED dose)
orders.instructions: Give 1,000 mg over 15 minutes IV Once.

orders.name: sodium chloride 0.9% 1,000 mL (main DKA fluid, no potassium)
orders.instructions: 500 mL/h 0300-0500, then 250 mL/h through the left forearm 18 g IV. When the D10W line starts (glucose under 250), lower to 150 mL/h. Riders are not subtracted. Continue unchanged on transfer.
orders.rationale: After the 1 L bolus: 500 mL/h (6.6 mL/kg/h) x2 hours, then 250 mL/h (3.3 mL/kg/h). No potassium while K is over 5.0, and peripheral IVs only, so potassium is given as riders.

orders.name: DKA PROTOCOL (adult, fixed-rate insulin): insulin rules, dextrose table, hypoglycemia rule, peripheral potassium table
orders.instructions: INSULIN: FIXED RATE 0.1 unit/kg/h = 7.6 units/h (weight 76.0 kg). No bolus. Do not titrate to glucose. Lower to 3.8 units/h (0.05 unit/kg/h) only if glucose is under 70, or under 150 while D10W runs at 150 mL/h (and call). HOLD only if K is under 3.5 (and call). Never stop the insulin for a low glucose: give dextrose instead. DEXTROSE TABLE (insulin stays at 7.6 units/h): start D10W 100 mL/h when glucose is under 250 and lower the 0.9% sodium chloride to 150 mL/h. Glucose 150-249 = 100 mL/h. Under 150 on 100 mL/h = 150 mL/h and call. Under 150 on 150 mL/h = lower insulin to 3.8 units/h and call. 250-299 on D10W = 50 mL/h. 300 or more = off and call. D10W is OFF whenever the insulin is held. It continues as long as IV insulin runs. HYPOGLYCEMIA ON THE INFUSION (glucose under 70): 50-69 and alert = dextrose 50% 12.5 g (25 mL) IV push; under 50 or not alert = 25 g (50 mL). Recheck in 15 minutes and repeat until 100 or more. Lower insulin to 3.8 units/h. Trace the dextrose line from bag to patient. Call. Do not stop the insulin. PERIPHERAL POTASSIUM PROTOCOL (peripheral IVs only): NO potassium in any bag. Give potassium as KCl 10 mEq in 100 mL riders over 1 hour on a pump (10 mEq/h), ONE at a time, at most 4 in a row, then recheck. Riders run in the right-arm IV. Never run a rider on a potassium-containing carrier. Give only if urine is at least 0.5 mL/kg/h (38 mL/h). By the NEWEST potassium: over 5.0 = none, recheck with the next set; 4.5-5.0 = 10 mEq this 4-hour cycle; 4.0-4.4 = 20 mEq; 3.5-3.9 = 30 mEq; UNDER 3.5 = HOLD the insulin infusion and the D10W, call the provider, give 4 riders back to back (40 mEq), 12-lead ECG, STAT potassium after the second rider has finished; restart insulin when K is 3.5 or more. Never draw labs from an arm with a running infusion. MAGNESIUM: call for Mg under 1.8. RESOLUTION: beta-hydroxybutyrate under 0.6 AND (venous pH 7.3 or more OR bicarbonate 18 or more); glucose is not a criterion.
orders.rationale: ADA/EASD/JBDS/AACE/DTS 2024 hyperglycemic crises consensus (adult).

notes.author: B. Kessel, RN
notes.summary: 28-year-old man with type 1 diabetes, 5 days of flu-like illness, vomiting, fast deep breathing; skipped his long-acting insulin 2 nights. Mask on; droplet precautions ordered. POC glucose 524.
notes.body:
**Arrival 0130** with his sister, Tessa Mercer (support person). Surgical mask placed at the door (cough, fever).

**Triage 0135**
T 100.6 F, HR 124, BP 102/60, RR 28 deep and regular (Kussmaul), SpO2 97% on room air. Pain 6/10 (belly and body aches). GCS 15 but drowsy. Weight 76.0 kg (ED bed scale). POC glucose 0138: **524**.

**History (patient and sister)**
- Type 1 diabetes since age 16. Injections: glargine 24 units at bedtime and lispro with meals. No pump, no sensor.
- Sore throat, dry cough, fever and body aches since Wednesday 01/06. Ate very little from Thursday.
- **Skipped his glargine Saturday and Sunday night**: "I wasn't eating, so I thought I'd go low." No lispro since Friday lunch. Last insulin of any kind: glargine Friday 2100.
- Vomited 6-8 times since Sunday about 1000. Belly ache. Very thirsty, urinating a lot. Meter read "HI" Sunday evening. No ketone check (his strips are expired).
- Sister texted him from 2100 with no answer. She used her key at about 0100 and found him drowsy, breathing fast and deep, "smelling like nail polish remover."

**Allergy:** codeine (hives).

**Plan per Dr. Lindahl (0140):** droplet precautions (respiratory viral panel to be sent), labs, ECG, chest x-ray, NPO. ESI level 2.

notes.summary: Sinus tachycardia 122, PR 146 ms, QRS 90 ms, QT/QTc 300/428 ms. Peaked, narrow T waves V2-V4 (potassium 5.6 at 0145).
notes.body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 122 bpm. PR 146 ms. QRS 90 ms. QT/QTc 300/428 ms (Bazett: RR 60/122 = 0.492 s; 0.300 / 0.701 = 0.428).

**Interpretation**
Sinus tachycardia. Tall, narrow, peaked T waves in V2 to V4. P waves present; PR and QRS normal (no signs of severe hyperkalemia). No ST changes. No arrhythmia.

**Context**
DKA. Potassium 5.6 at 0145. Acidosis and no insulin move potassium out of the cells; total body potassium is low. Insulin will move it back in: watch the potassium closely once the insulin starts.

notes.title: ED Provider Note - Diabetic Ketoacidosis
notes.author: F. Lindahl, MD
notes.summary: Moderate-to-severe DKA (pH 7.18, bicarbonate 8, anion gap 28, BHB 6.4) from basal insulin omission during a viral illness. 1 L bolus, 0.9% saline 500 mL/h, insulin 7.6 units/h from 0305 (K 5.6, so no potassium yet). Viral panel pending; droplet precautions. Admit to step-down.
notes.body:
**Chief complaint**
Vomiting, belly ache and fast breathing after 5 days of a flu-like illness.

**HPI**
28-year-old man with type 1 diabetes since age 16 on injections (glargine 24 units at 2100, lispro with meals). Sore throat, dry cough, fever and body aches since Wednesday. Ate little from Thursday. **Skipped glargine Saturday and Sunday night** because he was not eating and feared a low; no lispro since Friday lunch. Vomiting 6-8 times since Sunday morning. Sister found him drowsy and breathing fast at about 0100.

**Exam (0135)**
T 100.6 F, HR 124, BP 102/60, RR 28 Kussmaul, SpO2 97% room air. Drowsy, GCS 15, oriented. Fruity breath. Dry, cracked lips; skin tents. Lungs clear. Heart fast and regular. Abdomen soft, diffusely tender, no guarding or rebound. No rash.

**Results (0145)**
- Glucose 538. Na 131 (corrected 138.0). **K 5.6.** Cl 95. **CO2 8. Anion gap 28.** BUN 26. **Creatinine 1.5** (baseline 0.9). Mg 2.2. Phos 5.6.
- **BHB 6.4.** Venous gas: **pH 7.18**, pCO2 19, HCO3 6.8. Winter's expected pCO2 1.5 x 6.8 + 8 = 18.2 (16.2-20.2): compensation appropriate. Lactate 2.4.
- Effective osmolality 292 (no hyperosmolar overlap). Measured osmolality 304 vs calculated 301: osmolal gap 3.
- WBC 17.8 (no bands; stress and ketosis), Hgb 16.4, Hct 49.0. Lipase 92 (under 3 times normal; common in DKA). Liver tests normal; albumin 4.7.
- UA: glucose 4+, ketones large, no signs of infection.
- ECG 0200: sinus tachycardia 122, peaked T waves V2-V4, QTc 428.
- Chest x-ray: no pneumonia.
- POC glucose 0300 468 (after 1 L, before insulin), 0400 412.

**Assessment**
**Moderate-to-severe DKA** (pH 7.18 moderate; bicarbonate 8 severe; drowsy) from **stopping basal insulin during a viral illness**. The gap rose by 16 (28 - 12) and the bicarbonate fell by 16 (24 - 8): a pure anion-gap acidosis. Prerenal AKI. Influenza-like illness; respiratory viral panel pending.

**Plan (adult protocol, ADA/EASD/JBDS/AACE/DTS 2024 consensus)**
1. 0.9% sodium chloride 1 L over 1 hour (done 0155-0255), then 500 mL/h x2 hours, then 250 mL/h.
2. **Insulin 0.1 unit/kg/h = 7.6 units/h, fixed rate, no bolus**, started 0305 (K 5.6 is over 3.5).
3. Potassium: none while K is over 5.0; recheck with the 0500 labs. Peripheral IVs only.
4. Droplet precautions until the respiratory viral panel results.
5. Acetaminophen for fever; ondansetron for nausea.
6. Admit to step-down with telemetry (Dr. Varga).

**HPI**
Caleb Mercer is a 28-year-old man with type 1 diabetes since 2014 (age 16, diagnosed in DKA). One prior DKA at age 21 (missed insulin at college). Sore throat, dry cough, fever to 101.8 F and body aches since Wednesday 01/06. Poor appetite Thursday and Friday. Took glargine Friday 2100. **Skipped glargine Saturday and Sunday** ("no food, no insulin, or I'll go low"). Meter 380 Saturday night; "HI" Sunday evening. Vomited 6-8 times from Sunday about 1000. No ketone check (strips expired). His sister found him drowsy at about 0100.

**Past history**
Type 1 diabetes on injections, no pump, no sensor (declined one in 2025). HbA1c 8.1% (10/2026). Eye exam and urine albumin normal in 2026. Feels his lows (shaky, sweaty). Seasonal allergies.

**Home medicines**
Insulin glargine 24 units SubQ at 2100. Insulin lispro with meals: 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate + 1 unit per 50 mg/dL above 150. Acetaminophen 1,000 mg every 6 hours as needed. Loratadine 10 mg daily as needed. Glucagon nasal powder 3 mg as needed.

**Allergy:** codeine (hives).

**Social**
IT help-desk technician (works from home 3 days a week; employer insurance). Lives in an apartment with a roommate, Devin Szabo (works nights, training as a paramedic; away this weekend). Sister Tessa Mercer (31) lives 15 minutes away: support person and emergency contact. Parents out of state. Recreational soccer. Alcohol 2-4 drinks a week, none this week. No tobacco or drugs.

**Family history**
Maternal uncle: type 1 diabetes. Mother: hypothyroidism.

**Exam (0545)**
HR 114, BP 108/64, RR 24 deep, SpO2 98% room air, T 99.6 F (0500). Drowsy but answers. Fruity breath. Dry mucous membranes; skin tents. Lungs clear. Heart regular, fast. Abdomen soft, diffusely tender, no guarding. Moves all limbs. Height 180 cm, weight 76.0 kg (BMI 23.5); usual weight 79.0 kg.

**Results**
- 0145: glucose 538, Na 131 (corrected 138.0), K 5.6, Cl 95, CO2 8, anion gap 28, BUN 26, creatinine 1.5, BHB 6.4, pH 7.18, pCO2 19. Effective osmolality 292. WBC 17.8, no bands. Lipase 92. UA ketones large, no infection.
- 0500: glucose 348, Na 134, **K 4.6**, Cl 101, CO2 10, anion gap 23, creatinine 1.3, Mg 2.0, phos 3.8, BHB 5.5, pH 7.23, pCO2 22. Lactate 1.5.
- POC glucose 0500 354, 0600 302 (falling about 50-60 an hour).
- ECG: sinus tachycardia, peaked T waves (K 5.6). Chest x-ray clear.

**Assessment**
1. **Moderate-to-severe DKA** (pH 7.18, bicarbonate 8, BHB 6.4), trigger: stopped basal insulin during a viral illness. Improving on fluids and insulin.
2. **Potassium shift**: 5.6 -> 4.6 on insulin. Total body potassium is low; expect it to keep falling.
3. Prerenal AKI (creatinine 1.5 -> 1.3).
4. Influenza-like illness, respiratory viral panel pending. WBC 17.8 is from stress and ketosis (no bands, clear chest x-ray, clean urine).
5. Lipase 92: not pancreatitis (under 3 times normal).
6. Knowledge gap: no written sick-day plan.

**Plan**
- Step-down with telemetry, SD-3. Full Code.
- **DKA protocol (fixed rate)**: insulin 7.6 units/h; D10W 100 mL/h and 0.9% sodium chloride 150 mL/h when glucose is under 250; POC glucose every hour; hold insulin only if K is under 3.5.
- **Potassium**: peripheral IVs only, KCl riders per the protocol table by the newest potassium (one at a time, 10 mEq/h maximum).
- Labs: venous gas, BMP, Mg, phos, BHB at 0930, 1400, 2130, 0130, 0530. Replace Mg if under 1.8. Phosphate monitored. No bicarbonate (pH over 7.0).
- No pharmacologic VTE prophylaxis: age 28, walking, no clot risk factor.
- Hold home glargine and lispro while on the infusion. Transition when DKA resolves (BHB under 0.6 and pH 7.3 or more or bicarbonate 18 or more).
- Consults: endocrinology, pharmacy, diabetes educator, dietitian.

notes.title: Pharmacy Note - Medication History and DKA Protocol Check
notes.author: N. Bjork, PharmD
notes.summary: Medication history: glargine 24 units at 2100 (last Fri 2100), lispro 1:10 and 1:50 above 150; codeine allergy. Peripheral potassium limits reviewed. Ondansetron fine at QTc 428; recheck if K falls. His glucagon and blood ketone strips are expired.
notes.body:
**Sources:** patient, sister, pharmacy fill history, his pens and meter (brought by his sister).

**Home medicines**
- Insulin glargine 24 units SubQ once daily at 2100. Last dose **Fri 01/08 2100**; skipped Saturday and Sunday.
- Insulin lispro pen with meals: 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate + 1 unit per 50 mg/dL above 150. None since Friday lunch.
- Total daily dose about 46 units (24 basal + about 22 bolus) = 46 / 76 = 0.6 unit/kg/day.
- Acetaminophen 1,000 mg every 6 hours as needed (last Sunday 1000, vomited).
- Loratadine 10 mg daily as needed.
- **Glucagon nasal powder 3 mg: expired 06/2025.**
- **Blood ketone strips: expired 2024.** His meter can read blood ketones but he has no in-date strips. No refills of either on his pharmacy profile.

**Allergy:** codeine (hives).

**DKA protocol check (weight 76.0 kg)**
- Insulin 0.1 x 76.0 = 7.6 units/h (bag 1 unit/mL = 7.6 mL/h). Correct.
- D10W 100 mL/h = 10 g dextrose per hour; 150 mL/h = 15 g per hour.
- **Peripheral potassium:** no more than 10 mEq per hour, as KCl 10 mEq/100 mL riders over 1 hour, one at a time, at most 4 in a row. No more than 20 mEq/L in a peripheral bag (40 mEq/L is the central-line cap). All sources add up toward the 10 mEq/h limit. Lactated Ringer's carries 4 mEq/L.
- Ondansetron: fine at QTc 428. Recheck the QTc before more doses if potassium falls.
- Acetaminophen: maximum 3 g per day from all sources (1,000 mg IV given 0230).

**Recommendation:** review the expired supplies before discharge.

notes.title: Endocrinology Consult - DKA After Stopping Basal Insulin
notes.author: P. Beaumont, MD
notes.summary: Cause: he stopped his basal insulin while not eating. Early basal insulin on the drip is an option, but he will get his home glargine 24 units at the transition in the morning, with the drip stopped at least 2 hours later; keep morning dosing after that. Written sick-day plan and teaching before discharge; offer a sensor.
notes.body:
**Reason for consult**
DKA in type 1 diabetes. Requested by Dr. Varga.

**History**
Type 1 diabetes for 12 years on glargine 24 units at bedtime and lispro (1 unit/10 g, correction 1 unit/50 above 150). HbA1c 8.3% today (8.1% in 10/2026). No written sick-day plan: he says he "was told once, years ago." During this illness he stopped glargine because he was not eating. Followed by J. Harlow, MD.

**Data**
0930: anion gap 20, BHB 4.1, pH 7.27, K 3.9, Mg 1.8. Insulin 7.6 units/h with D10W.

**Impression**
DKA from **basal insulin omission** during a viral illness. Basal insulin covers the liver's glucose and ketone production all day, eating or not; without it, ketones rise within hours. Type 1 diabetes needs basal insulin every day, even when sick and not eating.

**Recommendations**
1. Continue the fixed-rate protocol until resolution (BHB under 0.6 and pH 7.3 or more or bicarbonate 18 or more).
2. **Transition:** early basal insulin while on the drip is an option, but he will get his **home glargine 24 units at the transition in the morning**, with the insulin infusion stopped **at least 2 hours later** (2024 consensus: 2-4 hours). Keep morning dosing after that (new time of day).
3. Lispro with meals at his home ratio and correction.
4. Written sick-day plan before discharge (extra lispro by blood ketones; total daily dose 46 units) and teaching with the diabetes educator.
5. Offer a glucose sensor referral.
6. Follow-up with Dr. Harlow after discharge.

**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 98 bpm. PR 150 ms. QRS 88 ms. QT/QTc 360/460 ms (Bazett: RR 0.612 s; 0.360 / 0.782 = 0.460).

**Interpretation**
Sinus rhythm. Low, flat T waves with U waves after them, best in V2 and V3. Two premature ventricular complexes on the strip. Compared with 0200: rate slower (122 to 98), the peaked T waves are gone and a low-potassium pattern has appeared.

**Context**
Potassium 5.6 (0145), 4.6 (0500), 3.9 (0930), 3.2 (1400) on the insulin infusion; magnesium 1.6. Insulin and D10W held at 1500; KCl riders one at a time; magnesium sulfate 2 g. Avoid ondansetron and other QT-prolonging drugs until K and QTc improve.

notes.title: Hospital Medicine Event Note - Potassium 3.2
notes.author: H. Ashworth, MD
notes.summary: Called by the RN at 1500 for K 3.2 (1445): insulin and D10W held per protocol, 4 KCl riders, magnesium sulfate 2 g (Mg 1.6), STAT labs 1720 after the second rider; avoid ondansetron until K and QTc are better.
notes.body:
**Event**
RN called at 1500: **K 3.2** on the 1400 labs (resulted 1445). Monitor showing flat T waves, U waves and PVCs. Calf cramps, legs heavy.

**1400 labs**
Na 137, K 3.2, Cl 106, CO2 13, anion gap 18, creatinine 1.0, glucose 198, **Mg 1.6**, phos 1.9. BHB 2.6. pH 7.29, pCO2 27.

**ECG 1505**
Sinus rhythm 98, flat T waves, U waves V2-V3, 2 PVCs, QTc 460 ms.

**Assessment**
Hypokalemia on insulin (K under 3.5) with low magnesium. Insulin moves potassium into the cells; low Mg makes K hard to correct.

**Plan**
- **Insulin infusion and D10W held** (RN held at 1500 per protocol). 0.9% sodium chloride 150 mL/h continues.
- **KCl riders x4 back to back** from 1505, one at a time (10 mEq/h, the peripheral limit).
- **Magnesium sulfate 2 g IV over 2 hours** (1515), left line.
- **STAT venous gas, BMP, Mg, BHB at 1720**, after the second rider and the magnesium finish, from the opposite arm.
- Restart insulin 7.6 units/h when K is 3.5 or more. Ketones will rise while insulin is held, so keep the hold short.
- Avoid ondansetron until K and QTc are better.
- Telemetry; hourly POC glucose.

notes.title: Hospital Medicine Note - Insulin Restarted
notes.author: H. Ashworth, MD
notes.summary: STAT K 3.6 (1745): insulin restarted 1750. BHB rose 2.6 -> 3.1 and pH 7.27 during the hold (expected). D10W back when glucose is under 250.
notes.body:
**STAT labs 1720**
Na 137, **K 3.6**, Cl 106, CO2 13, anion gap 18, creatinine 0.9, glucose 270, **Mg 2.0**, phos 2.0. **BHB 3.1.** pH 7.27, pCO2 28.

**Assessment and plan**
- **K 3.6** after 20 mEq with the insulin off: **insulin restarted 7.6 units/h at 1750**.
- **BHB rose 2.6 -> 3.1 and pH fell 7.29 -> 7.27** during the hold: without insulin the body makes ketones again. Expected; it should turn around now.
- D10W back on when glucose is under 250 (dextrose table).
- The 4th rider (1805) finishes the run of four; after that, potassium per protocol from the 2130 labs.
- Mg 2.0 after replacement. Creatinine 0.9: AKI resolved.
- If he keeps drinking well, lower the 0.9% sodium chloride to 100 mL/h at 1900.

notes.title: Night Hospitalist Note - Sign-Out and IV Infiltration
notes.author: G. Varga, MD
notes.summary: Sign-out received. RN reported the right antecubital IV infiltrated at 1900 during the 4th KCl rider (grade 2; stopped, removed, elevated, marked; new right forearm IV 1915). Site check every 2 hours. Next potassium per the 2130 labs.
notes.body:
**Sign-out from Dr. Ashworth**
DKA on fixed-rate insulin 7.6 units/h (restarted 1750 after a hold for K 3.2). STAT 1720: K 3.6, BHB 3.1, pH 7.27.

**Event (RN call 1905)**
At 1900 the right antecubital IV was **swollen about 4 cm, cool, pale, taut and burning** during the 4th KCl rider (92 of 100 mL infused). **Infiltration, INS grade 2.** The RN stopped the rider, disconnected, aspirated, removed the IV, elevated the arm, marked the edges and applied a cold pack per policy. About 9 mEq of potassium went into the tissue. New 20 g IV in the right forearm at 1915.

**Exam 2020**
Right elbow: swelling about 3 cm, soft, edges marked, no blisters, radial pulse 2+, fingers warm, moves them well.

**Plan**
- Site check every 2 hours; elevate on a pillow; call for blisters, skin color change, numbness or worse pain.
- Riders in the new right forearm IV per protocol from the 2130 labs; check the site every hour while a rider runs.
- D10W restarted at 1900 per the dextrose table; 0.9% sodium chloride 100 mL/h.

notes.title: Night Hospitalist Addendum - Maintenance Fluid Order
notes.author: G. Varga, MD
notes.summary: RN called about the 2245 KCl 40 mEq/L bag: peripheral IVs only, limit 20 mEq/L and no stacking with riders. Order discontinued. Plain 0.9% saline 100 mL/h and riders per protocol.
notes.body:
**Call from the RN at 2300**
At 2245 I ordered 0.9% sodium chloride with KCl 40 mEq/L at 100 mL/h to replace the plain saline. The RN did not hang it and called: Caleb has **peripheral IVs only**. The peripheral limit is **20 mEq/L in a bag** (40 mEq/L is a central-line strength). And 40 mEq/L at 100 mL/h = 4 mEq/h from the bag + 10 mEq/h from a rider = **14 mEq/h, over the 10 mEq/h peripheral limit**.

**Action**
Order discontinued at 2320. Keep plain 0.9% sodium chloride 100 mL/h and KCl riders per protocol (K 3.7 at 2130: 30 mEq this cycle, riders 2230, 2330, 0030).

**2130 labs**
Na 139, K 3.7, Cl 108, CO2 15, anion gap 16, glucose 196, Mg 1.9, phos 2.1. BHB 2.0. pH 7.31, pCO2 30. **Not resolved**: pH is over 7.3 but BHB is not under 0.6. Continue insulin and D10W.

notes.title: Night Hospitalist Event Note - Low Glucose on the Infusion
notes.author: G. Varga, MD
notes.summary: Called 0215 for glucose 112 (D10W raised to 150 per the table). At 0300 glucose 62: the D10W tubing had come apart at the Y-site connector when he got up at about 0100, and the dextrose ran into the bed. Dextrose 50% 12.5 g, recheck 124; insulin 3.8 units/h; new D10W tubing at 150 mL/h. Sitting at the edge of the bed, sweaty; no fall.
notes.body:
**0215 call**
RN called for glucose 112 at 0200 (158 at 0100). D10W had been raised to 150 mL/h at 0210 per the dextrose table. Plan then: keep insulin 7.6 units/h, recheck in 1 hour.

**0300 event**
Glucose **62**. Found sitting on the edge of the bed with the bed alarm sounding, sweaty, shaky and "foggy," wanting to walk to the bathroom. **No fall.** The RN traced the lines: the **D10W secondary tubing had pulled apart at the needleless connector on the Y-site**, probably when he got up to void at about 0100. The pump kept running with no alarm, and the dextrose dripped into the bed (sheet and gown wet).

**Treatment (RN, per protocol)**
- Dextrose 50% 12.5 g (25 mL) IV push 0305. Glucose **124 at 0315**.
- Insulin lowered to **3.8 units/h** (0.05 unit/kg/h) at 0305. **Not stopped**: BHB 1.1 and anion gap 14 on the 0130 labs, so ketones are still clearing.
- Open tubing end clamped; **new sterile D10W tubing at 150 mL/h** at 0310 (the contaminated end was not reconnected).
- Linen changed; back to bed; bed alarm reset.

**0130 labs**
Na 139, K 4.0, Cl 109, CO2 16, anion gap 14, glucose 140, Mg 1.9. BHB 1.1. pH 7.32, pCO2 31. Chloride 109 with CO2 16 and a gap of only 14: part of the low bicarbonate is now a non-gap acidosis from the saline.

**Plan**
Insulin 3.8 units/h, D10W 150 mL/h, glucose every hour, call if under 100. Potassium per protocol (K 4.0: 20 mEq, riders 0330 and 0430). Labs 0530.

notes.title: Night Hospitalist Note - DKA Resolved
notes.author: G. Varga, MD
notes.summary: 0530 labs: BHB 0.4, pH 7.34, HCO3 18, gap 13: DKA resolved. Transition to subcutaneous insulin this morning (the night NP will write the orders).
notes.body:
**0530 labs**
Na 139, **K 4.2**, Cl 108, **CO2 18**, **anion gap 13**, BUN 10, creatinine 0.8, glucose 160, Mg 1.9, phos 2.6. **BHB 0.4.** Venous gas **pH 7.34**, pCO2 34, HCO3 17.6.

**Assessment**
- **DKA resolved**: BHB 0.4 (under 0.6) AND pH 7.34 (7.3 or more); serum bicarbonate 18.
- Glucose stable on insulin 3.8 units/h and D10W 150 mL/h since the 0300 low (see event note).
- K 4.2: 20 mEq per protocol while the infusion runs.
- Weight 79.3 kg (0600, I&O record) from 76.0 on arrival; drinking well.

**Plan**
Transition to subcutaneous insulin this morning with breakfast. The night NP will write the orders. Endocrinology to review.

notes.title: Endocrinology Note - Transition to Subcutaneous Insulin
notes.author: P. Beaumont, MD
notes.summary: Corrected plan after the RN's question: glargine 24 units 0730 (now every morning), breakfast lispro 0800, drip and D10W off 0930 (2-hour overlap; D10W continues while IV insulin runs). No 2100 glargine tonight or at home.
notes.body:
**Call from the RN at 0700**
The RN asked about the 0635 order: glargine 24 units at 0700 **and** stop the insulin infusion, D10W and saline at 0700. IV insulin is gone within minutes, and glargine takes hours to start working: stopping both at the same time leaves him with no working insulin and risks ketones coming back.

**Data**
0530: BHB 0.4, pH 7.34, CO2 18, anion gap 13 (resolved). K 4.2. Eating breakfast at 0800.

**Plan**
1. **Insulin glargine 24 units SubQ at 0730** (his home dose), **then every morning at 0730** from now on.
2. **Insulin lispro with breakfast at 0800**: 1 unit per 10 g carbohydrate + correction 1 unit per 50 mg/dL above 150 (round to the nearest whole unit). Same with lunch (1200) and dinner (1730). Bedtime correction only if over 250.
3. **Keep the insulin infusion 3.8 units/h and D10W 150 mL/h until 0930** (at least 2 hours after glargine; 2024 consensus: 2-4 hours). D10W continues as long as IV insulin runs. Then stop both and the 0.9% saline (saline lock).
4. **No 2100 glargine tonight or at home**: the next dose is 0730 tomorrow.
5. BMP, Mg, phos and BHB at 0945, 1330 and 1730 (rebound check).
6. Diabetes educator today: written sick-day plan.
Orders to follow; the 0635 order will be discontinued.

notes.title: Hospital Medicine Progress Note - Day 2
notes.author: H. Ashworth, MD
notes.summary: Eating, walking, off the drip since 0930. Resume loratadine. Plan: one night on subcutaneous insulin, discharge tomorrow morning if stable.
notes.body:
**Subjective**
"I feel almost normal." Ate all of his breakfast. Showered. Mild dry cough. Sneezing (his usual allergies).

**Objective**
Glargine 24 units 0730, lispro with breakfast 0800. Insulin infusion, D10W and saline off at 0930; both IVs saline-locked. DKA resolved at 0530 (BHB 0.4, pH 7.34, CO2 18).

**Assessment and plan**
1. **DKA resolved**, now on glargine every morning and lispro with meals. Watch for rebound ketosis: labs at 0945.
2. Viral upper respiratory illness: afebrile, improving.
3. Seasonal allergies: resume home loratadine 10 mg daily as needed.
4. Up ad lib.
5. **Disposition:** one night on subcutaneous insulin, then discharge tomorrow morning if the overnight and fasting glucoses are stable and teaching is done.

notes.title: Nutrition Note - Carbohydrate Counting and Sick-Day Eating
notes.author: S. Pellegrino, RD
notes.summary: Carbohydrate counting review (accurate within 10 g on 3 of 4 items). Sick-day fluids and carbohydrate: 15 g per hour if not eating.
notes.body:
**Assessment**
Weight 79.3 kg (usual 79.0). Height 180 cm. Ate 100% of breakfast. Counts carbohydrate for his lispro at home; eats out at lunch on office days.

**Carbohydrate counting check**
Estimated 4 items from photos: correct within 10 g on 3 of 4 (overestimated a bagel by 20 g). Reviewed reading labels and serving sizes.

**Sick-day eating**

- If he cannot eat meals: **15 g carbohydrate every hour** (for example 4 oz regular juice, 1/2 cup regular soda, 1 regular ice pop, 6 saltine crackers) and keep taking his basal insulin.
- Sugar-free fluids when the glucose is over 250.

**Plan**
Consistent carbohydrate diet 60-75 g per meal in the hospital. Handout given.

notes.title: Hospital Medicine Addendum - 0945 Labs
notes.author: H. Ashworth, MD
notes.summary: 0945 labs: BHB 0.3 (no rebound), K 3.6: KCl ER 20 mEq at 1100 and 1500.
notes.body:
**0945 labs** (2 hours after glargine, 15 minutes after the drip stopped)
Na 138, **K 3.6**, Cl 106, CO2 20, **anion gap 12**, creatinine 0.8, glucose 182, Mg 1.8, phos 2.4. **BHB 0.3.** CBC: WBC 9.6, Hgb 13.8, platelets 241.

**Assessment and plan**

notes.title: Diabetes Education Session 1 - Written Sick-Day Plan
notes.author: W. Tamura, RN, CDCES
notes.summary: Taught Dr. Beaumont's written sick-day plan: never stop glargine; glucose and ketones every 2-4 hours when sick; extra lispro 5 units for ketones 0.6-1.4, 9 units and call for 1.5-2.9, ED for 3.0 or more; fluids; when to call. He still believed "no food, less long-acting."
notes.body:
**Learner:** Caleb (sister Tessa will join for session 2). Learns best with numbers and written steps.

**What happened**
He stopped glargine Saturday and Sunday because he was not eating. Explained: basal insulin covers the liver's glucose and ketone production all day, eating or not. Without it, ketones build up within hours.

**Written sick-day plan (Dr. Beaumont; total daily dose 46 units)**
- **Never stop glargine.** Take the full dose every morning.
- Check **glucose and blood ketones every 2-4 hours** when sick.
- Ketones **0.6-1.4**: extra lispro **5 units** (10% of 46), recheck glucose and ketones in 2 hours.
- Ketones **1.5-2.9**: extra lispro **9 units** (20% of 46), **call the diabetes team**, recheck in 2 hours.
- Ketones **3.0 or more**: **go to the ED.**
- Repeat the extra dose every 2-4 hours while ketones stay positive. Take it only if glucose is over 250 (or 150-250 with carbohydrate taken with it).
- Fluids 250 mL every hour (with 15 g carbohydrate per hour if not eating).
- Call for vomiting more than twice or cannot keep fluids down, glucose over 300 twice, or ketones not falling after extra insulin. ED for ketones 3.0 or more, fast breathing, belly pain or confusion.

**Response**
Listened and asked good questions, but at the end he said: "So if I'm not eating, I should still cut back the long-acting a bit?" He still believes "no food, less long-acting." Needs a second session with teach-back.

**Plan**
Session 2 this afternoon with his sister: teach-back of the plan, pen practice, ketone meter practice.
